# Dev-mode telemetry upload to dev server with automatic evaluation

**Priority:** high · **Issue type:** feature

## Problem statement

Recording a human play session for balance statistics (AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN) currently
requires the operator to discover and run the `npm run record` tool (which needs a
display + Playwright), or to manually dig a multi-megabyte string out of the player's
browser `localStorage` and paste it into a file (awkward, error-prone, size-limited).
There is no way to get telemetry from **any** browser hitting the dev server. We want a
dev-mode-only, zero-effort flow: the game itself collects the run, and at the end of
the game uploads the telemetry file to the server the game is running on; the server
stores it in `recordings/` and automatically runs the human evaluation on it.

None of this must be reachable when dev mode is not enabled (production builds, static
hosting, `vite preview`/`vite build` output).

## Users

- **As a maintainer**, I want any browser playing the dev-mode game to automatically
  deliver its recorded run telemetry to the dev server and have the human evaluation
  run on it, so I can collect balance statistics without any manual export step.
- **As a player/operator in dev mode**, I want telemetry collection to be controllable
  via a game setting (on by default), so I can opt out of upload without restarting the
  server.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Dev-only feature gate.** A fresh `npm run dev` game session (no special env vars)
   collected the run's telemetry by default and uploaded it at run end; the upload
   mechanism and the collection-on-by-default behaviour are unreachable in a
   production build. A dev-only enforcement test asserts no production call site /
   production bundle path can enable upload or collect-on-by-default.
- **Setting (on by default).** A new game setting, e.g. "Share telemetry with the dev
   server (dev mode)" in `SettingsScene`, persisted in the existing settings store,
   defaults to **on**. When off, the dev game neither collects nor uploads telemetry.
   The setting is inert (ignored) in non-dev builds.
- **Upload at end of game.** At run end (the existing `_finishRun`/run-end hook), and
   only when dev mode + setting on, the game POSTs the local JSONL sink's accumulated
   telemetry (`ai_hell_telemetry_jsonl`) to the dev server the page was served from
   (same-origin fetch; no change to production telemetry/consent config). The upload
   is fire-and-forget and must not block or crash the game.
- **Server-side receipt.** The dev server (Vite dev-only middleware, `apply: 'serve'`,
   mirroring `configCsvPlugin`) exposes an upload endpoint. On receipt it validates
   the body against the telemetry schema/recording reader, stores it in the
   `recordings/` folder using the existing `session-<timestamp>.jsonl` naming, and
   returns a confirmation. Malformed bodies are rejected (4xx) and never written.
- **Automatic evaluation.** After a valid recording is stored, the human evaluation
   pipeline runs automatically on it (the existing `--human` path producing
   `human-balance-report.json` and companions under an `eval-output/`-style location).
   The evaluation runs asynchronously so it never blocks the game or the upload
   response; its completion/summary is logged. The full existing `npm run record` /
   `npm run evaluate -- --human` flows continue to work unchanged.
- **Tests + docs.** Tests cover: the setting (default on, persistence, dev-only
   behaviour), the uploader (fires at run end with the sink content when dev+on,
   no-op otherwise), the server middleware (valid/invalid bodies, storage path, eval
   trigger, dev-only registration) and the dev-only enforcement scan. Docs
   (`docs/TELEMETRY.md`, `docs/dev/recording-and-replay.md`) describe the dev-mode
   auto-upload + automatic evaluation flow. Full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- **Dev-tooling only.** No production call site, no change to production
  telemetry/consent config (`VITE_TELEMETRY_CONSENT`, consent prompt). Production
  builds never collect or upload via this path.
- Reuse the existing telemetry framework sinks and record schema — no new recording
  mechanism, no schema divergence.
- The existing `ai_hell_telemetry_jsonl` local sink content is the canonical payload;
  the sink's localStorage content is left intact after upload (existing
  `npm run record` and inspection flows must keep working).
- No PII handling change: the payload is the same schema-only recording already
  written by the local dev sink.
- Same-origin upload (the page is served by the dev server), so no CORS work.
- Evaluation reuse: the shipped `scripts/evaluate.mjs --human` pipeline (and its
  `src/ai/eval/cli.ts` core) is invoked as-is rather than reimplemented.

## Existing state

- `src/telemetry/` — consent-gated framework; local dev sink writes JSONL to
  `localStorage` under `ai_hell_telemetry_jsonl`; disabled by default (`VITE_TELEMETRY_ENABLED`).
- `src/core/settingsStore.ts` — typed `SettingsRecord` persisted under
  `ai_hell_settings` (volume, mute, bindings); settings scene reads/writes it.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_finishRun()` (≈3262) is the run-end hook that already
  calls `runTelemetry.runEnd()` and emits the dev-gated run-ended signal.
- `vite.config.ts` + `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts` — the established dev-only
  middleware pattern (`apply: 'serve'`, Vite plugin with HTTP endpoints); a telemetry
  upload plugin should follow it.
- `scripts/recording.mjs` / `scripts/inspect-telemetry.mjs` — `parseRecording` /
  `parseTelemetryJsonl` for validating and splitting the flat record stream.
- `scripts/evaluate.mjs` + `src/ai/eval/cli.ts` — the `--human` evaluation pipeline
  (same-seed comparison + `human-balance-report.json` from the shared helper,
  AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN).
- `recordings/` is gitignored (dev play recordings, AH-0MUY08W7Y004GATZ).

## Desired change

1. New `SettingsRecord` field (e.g. `shareTelemetryDev: boolean`, default `true`),
   surfaced as a toggle in `SettingsScene`; inert unless `import.meta.env.DEV`.
2. In dev mode, when the setting is on, the game enables the local jsonl sink (the
   default dev config currently requires `VITE_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=true` — this feature
   makes a stock `npm run dev` collect when the setting is on) and, at `_finishRun()`,
   POSTs the sink's JSONL content to the dev server.
3. New dev-only Vite plugin (`vite/plugins/telemetryUploadPlugin.ts`, registered
   `apply: 'serve'`) exposing e.g. `POST /api/telemetry/upload`: validate → write
   `recordings/session-<timestamp>.jsonl` → trigger the human evaluation asynchronously
   (spawn `node scripts/evaluate.mjs --human <file> --out <eval-output>/uploaded/<ts>` or
   invoke the CLI core via SSR) → log the result.
4. Dev-only enforcement test (mirroring the existing human-stats scan) asserting neither
   the upload path nor the on-by-default collection is reachable from production
   sources/builds.
5. Docs update (`docs/TELEMETRY.md`, `docs/dev/recording-and-replay.md`).

## Key Files

- `src/core/settingsStore.ts` (+ `.test.ts`) — new setting field + default.
- `src/scenes/SettingsScene.ts` — dev-only toggle (place/naming to be confirmed at plan time).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — dev+setting gate at `_finishRun()`, uploader call.
- New uploader module (game-side, e.g. `src/telemetry/upload.ts` or
  `src/core/devTelemetryUpload.ts`) — dev-only, fetch + no-op otherwise, tested.
- `vite/plugins/telemetryUploadPlugin.ts` (+ `.test.ts`) — dev-only upload middleware +
  evaluation trigger.
- `vite.config.ts` — register the new dev-only plugin.
- `scripts/recording.mjs` / `scripts/inspect-telemetry.mjs` — payload validation reuse.
- `scripts/evaluate.mjs` + `src/ai/eval/cli.ts` — automatic evaluation trigger.
- `docs/TELEMETRY.md`, `docs/dev/recording-and-replay.md` — documentation.

## Related work

- **Collect balance statistics from human player games** (AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN) — the
  human `BalanceReport` the automatic evaluation produces; upstream motivation.
- **Dev recording, analysis and replay/ghost tooling** (AH-0MUY08W7Y004GATZ) — the
  recording path (`npm run record`, `parseRecording`) and `recordings/` folder.
- **Telemetry framework** (AH-0MUY08VJ9006BHJO / AH-0MUY08VVQ007HSSH) — record schema,
  sinks, consent gates this feature builds on.
- **Periodically validate the human experience** (AH-0MV7WVHU0000U775) — downstream
  consumer of human balance statistics this flow feeds.
- **configCsvPlugin** (AH-0MTZWZ9TE009CVUA) — dev-only middleware pattern to mirror.
- **Human balance-statistics test suite** (AH-0MV8ISNNY003FHQ7) — the test coverage the
  auto-evaluation flow should extend (found by automated related-work scan).
- **Realistic demo/attract bot framework + playtester telemetry** (AH-0MUY089KR003F8S4) —
  completed production-telemetry precedent; related but **not** a duplicate of this
  dev-mode-only auto-upload flow (found by automated related-work scan).
- Full automated related-work report: `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-AH-0MVBHRLY8004BGDN.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** dev-mode detection is `import.meta.env.DEV` (browser) and
  `apply: 'serve'` (server middleware); a production build/static host cannot reach
  the upload endpoint or on-by-default collection.
- **Assumption:** the payload is the local sink's accumulated JSONL and the sink is
  left intact after upload; repeated runs re-upload the whole accumulated stream
  (possible duplicate lines across sequential runs — mitigation: acceptable for dev
  data; a "capture window" or clear-after-upload can be negotiated at plan time).
- **Assumption:** uploads are validated with the existing recording reader
  (`parseTelemetryJsonl` semantics); only schema-valid records are stored.
- **Assumption:** automatic evaluation reuses the shipped `--human` pipeline
  (balance report + comparison artifacts) under a timestamped output directory; the
  exact trigger mechanism (child process vs in-process SSR) is an implementation
  decision assessed at plan time.
- **Risk:** enabling collection by default in stock `npm run dev` changes the
  telemetry gate's current "disabled unless env-flagged" default — must remain
  dev-mode-only, verifiable by the enforcement test and a production-build check.
- **Risk:** running Vite SSR evaluation inside the dev-server process could contend
  with the running server — prefer a spawned child process for the async evaluation.
- **Risk:** `npm run dev` currently opens a browser via `server.open` — unchanged;
  the uploader works from any browser (including a LAN/remote client) because the
  page and server are same-origin as served.
- **Scope guard (scope-creep risk):** enhancements such as a per-run "capture
  window", clear-after-upload, per-browser opt-out dashboards, or any
  production-facing variant are deliberately **out of scope** here; the first two
  are recorded as plan-time decisions and the rest would be new work items.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN** – Collect balance statistics from human player games (dev mode only) (completed)
- **AH-0MV8ISNNY003FHQ7** – Human balance-statistics test suite (completed)
- **AH-0MUY089KR003F8S4** – Realistic demo/attract bot framework + playtester telemetry (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: acceptance, accumulated, already, api, apply (+296 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: accumulated, already, api, apply, asserting (+270 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0mtzwz9te009cvua, accumulated, already, api, apply (+258 more)


## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

The seed context (operator-authored brief) was complete enough to draft directly;
no blocking clarifying questions were required. The entries below record the
decision points resolved from the repository/worklog rather than by interview.

- **Q: Is there an existing dev-only upload endpoint or uploader module to reuse?** —
  Answer (agent, repo search): No. `vite/plugins/` contains only `configCsvPlugin`;
  `src/telemetry/transport.ts` is the consent-gated framework transport, not a
  dev-server uploader. Conclusion: a new dev-only Vite plugin
  (`vite/plugins/telemetryUploadPlugin.ts`) + a game-side uploader module are
  required. Evidence: `vite/plugins/`, `src/telemetry/transport.ts`.
- **Q: Which run-end hook hosts the upload?** — Answer (agent, repo search):
  `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` `_finishRun()` (the existing run-end hook that already
  calls `runTelemetry.runEnd()`). Evidence: `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`.
- **Q: Reuse validation vs invent a parser?** — Answer (agent, repo search):
  Reuse `scripts/recording.mjs` `parseRecording` / `parseTelemetryJsonl` semantics.
  Evidence: `scripts/recording.mjs`, `scripts/inspect-telemetry.mjs`.
- **Q: Reuse the evaluation pipeline or reimplement?** — Answer (agent): Reuse the
  shipped `scripts/evaluate.mjs --human` pipeline / `src/ai/eval/cli.ts` as-is.
- **Q: Is this a duplicate of existing completed work?** — Answer (agent, worklog
  search): No. The automated scan surfaced (AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN),
  (AH-0MV8ISNNY003FHQ7) and (AH-0MUY089KR003F8S4), all related but addressing
  upstream/downstream or production-telemetry concerns; none provides the
  dev-mode-only auto-upload + auto-evaluation flow. Duplicate check performed — no
  overlapping completed item found.
- **Q: Exact trigger mechanism for the async evaluation (child process vs in-process
  SSR)?** — Answer (agent): **OPEN QUESTION (plan-time decision).** The brief's
  stated preference is a spawned child process to avoid contending with the running
  dev server; to be confirmed at plan time.
- **Q: Capture window / clear-after-upload semantics?** — Answer (agent): **OPEN
  QUESTION (plan-time decision).** Default in the brief is to leave the local sink
  intact and accept possible duplicate lines across sequential dev runs; a capture
  window or clear-after-upload is negotiable at plan time.
data.title: Dev-mode telemetry upload to dev server with automatic evaluation

# End-to-end acceptance verification (dev run + production build)

Child of **Dev-mode telemetry upload to dev server with automatic evaluation** (AH-0MVBHRLY8004BGDN).

## Goal

Verify all parent acceptance criteria on a real dev server run and a production build, and gate
the parent's completion on the evidence.

## User story

As a maintainer, I want proof that the whole flow works end-to-end in dev and is unreachable in
production before the parent feature is accepted.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Dev happy path:** stock `npm run dev` (no special env vars), play a run to completion;
  confirm a `recordings/session-*.jsonl` file appears, the background evaluation runs and its
  `human-balance-report.json` (+ companions) appear under the eval output dir, and the dev-server
  console logs the evaluation summary.
- **Opt-out path:** with the setting off in dev, confirm **no** new recording file and **no**
  upload request (game neither collects nor uploads).
- **Production check:** `npm run build` passes (incl. `tsc --noEmit`, `vite build` and
  `check-bundle-hygiene`); `vite preview` serves no upload endpoint; the enforcement scan (F1)
  and full project test suite pass via the project test skill.
- Evidence (screenshots/URLs, file listings, log excerpts, test output) is recorded as a comment
  on the parent work item with the final commit hash.

## Minimal implementation

- Manual dev-run + setting-off run + production build verification steps above.
- Run the full suite via the test skill; triage any failures into critical test-failure items
  per the triage policy.
- Record evidence and a completion comment on AH-0MVBHRLY8004BGDN.

**Key Files:**

- Evidence/logs referencing `recordings/session-*.jsonl`, the eval output dir, `dist/` bundle and test output.

## Dependencies

- F1–F7 (verification is the final slice).

## Deliverables

Verified acceptance evidence; parent ready for `in_review` only after this passes.

## Goal

Replace the arena's fixed two-to-N-wave hostile reservoir (skirmish model) with the **shared campaign sequencer**: the arena builds the shipped campaign via `buildSequencedLevels(rows, defaultCandidatePool, { seed })` (honouring `fixed`/`curve`/`dynamic` generation modes), drives the shared `WaveManager` state machine, spawns from `planSpawns(seededRng)`, gates wave/level completion through `onEnemyDestroyed`, and emits the canonical `wave_start`/`wave_cleared`/`level_cleared` telemetry events so `waveReached` and `levelReached` become meaningful, non-zero distributions in batch reports.

## User story

As a game designer, I want a bot batch to play the same campaign the game ships (all levels/waves via the shared sequencer), so per-wave difficulty targets can be tuned from evidence instead of intuition.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1:** One arena run plays the shared campaign (all levels and waves of the shipped definition, including `fixed`/`curve`/`dynamic` generation modes) and emits real `wave_start`/`wave_cleared`/`level_cleared` records with the canonical payloads from `runTelemetry.ts` (`level`, `waveNumber`, `waveCount`); a batch report shows non-zero `waveReached`/`levelReached`.
- **AC2:** Wave/level progression is driven exclusively by the shared `WaveManager` (`beginGame`, `planSpawns`, `onEnemyDestroyed`) and `buildSequencedLevels` — no divergent copy of campaign, wave, enemy or ship stats in src/ai/eval/ (asserted by the existing duplicate-body/parity guards).
- **AC3:** The `dynamic` wave mode derives from the run seed exactly as the game does (buildSequencedLevels `{ seed }`), so two runs with the same seed produce the same campaign for byte-identical telemetry.
- **AC4:** The Level-10 boss trigger is treated as the end of the run (no boss/mini-boss simulation this round — fidelity boundary, parent Q2=a); the boundary is documented in code.
- **AC5:** Determinism preserved: same seed + config + policy produces identical records on the campaign path; run never reads the wall clock.
- **AC6:** Unit tests cover progression, canonical event emission, seed-derived dynamic mode, and the no-divergent-copy guard; they pass under Node/vitest headless.

## Key Files

**Key Files:**
- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` — drive buildSequencedLevels + WaveManager; emit wave/level events
- `src/ai/eval/arena.test.ts` — campaign progression, event payloads, dynamic-mode seed tests
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — shared state machine consumed by the arena
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — shared campaign builder (fixed/curve/dynamic)
- `src/waves/Formations.ts` — static LEVELS skeleton merged by the builder
- `src/scenes/core/runTelemetry.ts` — canonical wave_start/wave_cleared/level_cleared event names
- `src/ai/eval/types.ts` — telemetry/types consumed by metrics (verify/keep)
data.title: Arena plays the shipped campaign through the shared WaveManager

## Goal

Model the mineral hold and the hold-full upgrade-choice loop in the arena using the **shared choice system** (`chooseOptions`/`randomChoiceStrategy` from src/powerups/choice.ts with the run's seeded RNG), so the arena emits `hold_full` and canonical `choice_selected` events and report `upgradesSelected` becomes a meaningful per-choice-id distribution. The bot picks among the offered options using the same seeded stream (parent Q1=a). Choices permanently affect the run (ownership context carried into later choice offers) via the headless-safe adapter identified in the spike child.

## User story

As the automated-balancing maintainer, I want the arena to exercise the same upgrade-choice flow the game ships, so per-upgrade balance can be measured from bot runs.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1:** A run collects minerals into a shared-model hold (`MineralHold` semantics: capacity, growth multiplier, overflow); when the hold fills, the arena offers options via shared `chooseOptions(3, randomChoiceStrategy, seededRng, context)` and emits `hold_full` with the offered option ids.
- **AC2:** The bot selects one offered option via the run's seeded RNG stream; the arena emits `choice_selected` with the canonical `{ index, id }` payload; a batch report shows non-zero per-choice-id `upgradesSelected` distributions.
- **AC3:** The reward is applied through the shared reward path (or the named headless adapter from the spike) so later choice offers carry accurate owned-weapon/power-up context (weapon-level/power-up-level options) — no invented option model in src/ai/eval/.
- **AC4:** Deterministic per seed: the same seed yields the same choice offers and selections (byte-identical telemetry).
- **AC5:** Unit tests cover hold-full triggering, canonical event payloads, ownership-context carry-over, and seeded determinism; they pass headless under Node/vitest.

## Key Files

**Key Files:**
- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` — mineral hold, choice offers, selection, choice_selected emission
- `src/ai/eval/arena.test.ts` — hold-full, event payloads, ownership context, determinism tests
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — shared chooseOptions/randomChoiceStrategy/buildChoiceCandidates
- `src/core/GameState.ts` — MineralHold semantics (capacity, growth, overflow)
- `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts` — applyMineralChoiceReward (headless adapter from spike)
- `src/scenes/core/runTelemetry.ts` — canonical hold_full/choice_selected event names
- `src/ai/eval/metrics.ts` — already parses choice_selected; verify/keep
- **AC6 (parent-AC2 traceability):** The bot makes upgrade selections through the shared upgrade-choice flow and `choice_selected` events are emitted; a batch report shows non-zero per-choice-id `upgradesSelected` distributions.
data.title: Arena resolves hold-full upgrade choices through the shared choice flow

## Goal

Make the full-campaign arena path the default in batch mode (parent Q3=b) and expose the config/CLI surface: `ArenaConfig`/`BatchConfig` gain a `campaign` surface defaulting to **true**, `scripts/evaluate.mjs` gains a `--skirmish` flag (and keeps `--batch`/`--games`/`--policies`/`--ticks`), a full-campaign run is bounded by a finite tick budget (higher default than the current 1800; `gameComplete`/death ends the run early), and the balance report's existing per-wave/per-level aggregation consumes the new events unchanged.

## User story

As the automated-balancing maintainer, I want `--batch` to automatically exercise the full shipped campaign, so the default report reflects what players experience without extra flags.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1:** `--batch` and `--games N` with no extra flags play full campaigns and the report shows non-zero `waveReached`/`levelReached`/`upgradesSelected` distributions.
- **AC2:** `--skirmish` opts back into the previous single-level skirmish path (backward compatible for existing consumers/tests).
- **AC3:** Campaign runs are finitely bounded — a configurable tick budget with a sane higher default, early exit on death or `gameComplete` (boss trigger); no unbounded simulation.
- **AC4:** Batch determinism preserved: same seeds + config + policies produce a byte-identical serialised balance report (`recordsHash` stable).
- **AC5:** Single-run evaluation (`runEvaluation`, A/B, human comparison) keeps the skirmish semantics and the difference is documented (report comparability note) — changed only by deliberate later work.
- **AC6:** CLI/engine/report unit tests cover the new defaults and both modes.

## Key Files

**Key Files:**
- `src/ai/eval/types.ts` — ArenaConfig/BatchConfig campaign surface (default true)
- `src/ai/eval/engine.ts` — runBatch campaign default + bounded tick budget
- `src/ai/eval/cli.ts` — --skirmish flag parsing, campaign surface in runConfig
- `scripts/evaluate.mjs` — shell flag wiring (--skirmish, default campaign)
- `src/ai/eval/engine.test.ts` — batch default/campaign/skirmish tests
- `src/ai/eval/cli.test.ts` — CLI flag tests
- `src/ai/eval/report.ts` — per-wave/per-level aggregation (verify unchanged)
data.title: Full-campaign batch runs by default with a bounded tick budget

## Goal

Verify the campaign arena path's three hard guarantees with acceptance tests, so the balance loop (AH-0MV8Q5EYE001R715) can trust the richer reports: byte-identical replay, config sensitivity (a `difficulty-curves.csv` edit or upgrade-definition edit measurably shifts the corresponding distributions for the same seeds), and no wall-clock/IO in the pure eval core (parent AC4/AC5/AC7).

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1:** A test replays the same seed + config + policy on the campaign path twice and asserts byte-identical records / stable `recordsHash`.
- **AC2:** A test edits a difficulty-curve row (e.g. raises a wave's `targetDifficulty`) and asserts the same seeds produce a measurably different `waveReached`/`levelReached` distribution.
- **AC3:** A test edits an upgrade definition and asserts the same seeds produce a measurably different `upgradesSelected` distribution.
- **AC4:** A guard test asserts the pure eval core (arena/metrics/engine) never imports a wall-clock or I/O module on its campaign path; campaign progression, upgrade-choice emission, single-source-of-truth, config sensitivity and determinism are all covered by unit tests (parent AC7 umbrella).
- **AC5:** All new tests pass headless under Node/vitest and run in the full suite.

## Key Files

**Key Files:**
- `src/ai/eval/arena.test.ts` — byte-identical replay + no-wall-clock guard tests
- `src/ai/eval/engine.test.ts` — recordsHash stability and config-sensitivity batch tests
- `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` — edit target difficulty for sensitivity test
- `src/powerups/types.ts` — POWER_UP_CATALOGUE (edit an upgrade definition for sensitivity test)
- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — weapon tuning (alternative upgrade-definition edit target)
- **AC6 (parent-AC4 traceability):** Same seed + config + policy ⇒ byte-identical campaign report; `recordsHash` stable; no wall-clock/IO in the pure eval core.
- **AC7 (parent-AC5 traceability):** Editing `difficulty-curves.csv` (e.g. raising a wave’s `targetDifficulty`) and/or an upgrade definition measurably changes the corresponding report distribution for the same seeds, verified by test.

## Goal

Adapt the existing eval test suite to the new campaign-by-default batch so the whole suite stays green and both modes remain covered: `arena.test.ts`, `engine.test.ts`, `cli.test.ts`, `balanceStats.test.ts`, `report.test.ts` (and any test asserting the old skirmish-only default). Also confirm the bot batch and human campaign runs (AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN) are directly comparable now that both carry wave/level/upgrade events.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1:** Every existing eval test that assumed a skirmish-only batch is updated (or explicitly scoped to `--skirmish`), and the full source/ai/eval test set passes.
- **AC2:** Both the campaign and skirmish paths are covered by their own tests (spawns, events, report shape for each).
- **AC3:** Where a test asserted `waveReached`/`levelReached`/`upgradesSelected` were empty, it now asserts meaningful non-zero values on the campaign path.
- **AC4:** Bott-vs-human balance-stat comparability is asserted (same schema, both populate wave/level/upgrade fields now) and documented in the relevant test comment.

## Key Files

**Key Files:**
- `src/ai/eval/arena.test.ts` — skirmish vs campaign spawns/events coverage
- `src/ai/eval/engine.test.ts` — batch-default assertions updated
- `src/ai/eval/cli.test.ts` — default/--skirmish CLI assertions updated
- `src/ai/eval/balanceStats.test.ts` — non-zero wave/level/upgrade expectations
- `src/ai/eval/report.test.ts` — report-shape expectations for both modes

## Goal

Document exactly what the headless arena now models (full campaign progression via the shared sequencer, hold-full upgrade choices) and what remains simplified (VFX, formations, mini-boss/boss, rendering), so consumers never over-read the balance report (parent AC6/AC9). # Pure scene-capture module: config parsing, validation and timing

The pure, browser-free core of the multi-scene capture feature (AH-0MUX2NLFZ00128WC): parses and validates the scene-list JSON config, derives the watchable gym scene set, builds the per-scene capture plan (including the two 0.25 s fades), and formats the `--json` payload. No server, browser or Playwright imports — fully hermetic and unit-tested, consumed by the capture driver (sibling item). A shared browser-free registry of watchable gym scene keys mirrors the existing `CAPTURE_SCENARIOS` parity pattern (`scripts/capture-scenarios.mjs`) so the CLI pre-boot validation and the page-side director agree on the same set.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Covers parent AC1.** A JSON config file specifies an ordered, arbitrary-length list of scenes; each entry carries a `target` (gym scene key), a `playMs` duration, a `captureMs` duration, and an optional `label`. The file is parsed and validated **before** any server/browser boots, failing fast with an actionable, non-zero-exit error for a missing/unreadable/malformed file, an unknown or unsupported `target`, an empty scene list, or a non-positive/non-numeric `playMs`/`captureMs` (mirroring the existing `--count` validation style).
- **Watchable target set.** The watchable gym scene set is derived from the discovered gym scenes minus the parameterised `GymFodderEnemies` and `GymLevel`; unknown or unsupported targets are rejected.
- **Scene-plan builder.** A pure builder computes per-scene `{ target, playMs, captureMs, startMs, endMs }`, inserting the two 0.25 s fades (`SCENE_FADE_MS = 250`) between consecutive scenes; exported, side-effect-free, deterministic.
- **JSON payload builder.** A pure builder reports per-scene timings, the total output duration and the output path.
- **Tests green.** The test-first sibling suite (`Tests: scene-capture config, timing and director keys`) passes; `scripts/capture-scenes.d.mts` declares the exported types.

## Key Files

- `scripts/capture-scenes.mjs` (new)
- `scripts/capture-scenes.d.mts` (new)
- `scripts/capture-scenes.test.ts` (sibling test item)
- `scripts/capture-scenarios.mjs` (shared browser-free registry parity pattern)
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` (`parseCaptureCount` validation style reference)
- `src/utils/gymDiscovery.ts` (discovered gym scene key convention, `Gym<Name>`)

## Minimal Implementation

1. New shared browser-free registry exported from this module: `WATCHABLE_GYM_SCENE_KEYS` (the discovered non-parameterised gym keys) and `SCENE_FADE_MS = 250`, following the `CAPTURE_SCENARIOS` parity pattern so the CLI and the director read one source of truth.
2. `parseSceneConfig` / `validateSceneConfig`: read + validate the JSON, reusing the `--count` error style; throw a typed error carrying an actionable message and a non-zero exit mapping.
3. Watchable-set validation against the registry; reject unknown/parameterised targets (`GymFodderEnemies`, `GymLevel`).
4. `buildScenePlan(scenes)`: per-scene `startMs`/`endMs` with the two fades between consecutive scenes; total duration.
5. `buildScenesPayload(...)`: the `--json` shape (per-scene timings + total duration + output path).
6. `scripts/capture-scenes.d.mts` type declarations matching the project's `.d.mts` convention.

## Dependencies

- Test-first sibling item (its tests define the contract).

## Deliverables

- Hermetic config/validation/planning module + types, consumed by the capture driver and the director.

# Multi-scene capture driver: one recorder, fades, single WebM

The orchestrator slice of the multi-scene capture feature (AH-0MUX2NLFZ00128WC): boots one dev server + one browser, drives the in-page director and the page-side fade overlay, records every scene with a single `MediaRecorder`, and writes exactly one WebM plus the `--json` payload. Reuses the existing capture machinery (server boot, mime selection, audio tap, probe, progress) rather than duplicating it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Covers parent AC3.** A single `MediaRecorder` captures the scenes in config order; between consecutive scenes a page-side canvas overlay fades **to** black over 0.25 s then **from** black over 0.25 s before the next scene's play window, and the fade is present in the recorded video (the recorder captures the overlay). The scene count is arbitrary (verified with at least three scenes).
- **Covers parent AC4.** The command writes exactly **one** WebM (`video/webm;codecs=vp9,opus`, falling back per the existing `resolveCaptureMimeType` order) containing all scenes plus their transitions at 960×540 with the game's own SFX, and the result passes the existing non-trivial video+audio probe. The `--json` payload reports per-scene `{ target, playMs, captureMs, startMs, endMs }` timings and the total output duration/file path.
- **Entry point.** `npm run capture:scenes -- --config <file>` is the documented CLI entry point; the config is parsed and validated before any server or browser boots.
- **Reuse.** Reuses the existing pure capture machinery (Vite server boot, headless Chromium, mime selection, audio tap, probe, progress) rather than duplicating it.
- **Fade injection.** Playwright injects the fade overlay and calls the director between scenes; the recorder and page are never reloaded across the batch.

## Key Files

- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` (expose/reuse the server-boot, browser, recorder and probe plumbing, or add a `--scenes` mode)
- `scripts/capture-scenes.mjs` (sibling pure module — config/plan/payload)
- `scripts/capture-scenes.d.mts` / `scripts/capture-scenes.test.ts` (siblings)
- `src/core/captureDirector.ts` (sibling director for in-page scene switching)
- `package.json` (`capture:scenes` script)
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` (documented by the docs item)

## Minimal Implementation

1. Add a `--scenes <config>` mode (or a small sibling orchestrator) reusing the `runCaptureSession`-style server/browser boot and recorder/probe plumbing.
2. Before any boot: parse + validate the config via the pure module; map validation errors to a non-zero exit with an actionable message.
3. One page + one `MediaRecorder`: for each scene, start the gym scene via the director, play for `playMs`, record while capturing for `captureMs`; between scenes inject the page-side fade overlay (fade-to-black 250 ms, then fade-from-black 250 ms) so the recorder captures the transition.
4. Stop the recorder, run the existing probe (`isNonTrivialClip` / `evaluateAudioTrack` / `combineClipVerdict`), and write the single WebM to the configured output path (default under the gitignored `capture-output/` tree).
5. Emit the `--json` payload (per-scene timings + total duration + path); progress reporting reuses `formatProgress`.
6. Register `npm run capture:scenes` in `package.json`.

## Dependencies

- Pure config/planning module (sibling).
- Dev-gated director (sibling) for in-page scene switching.
- (Both of those depend on the test-first item.)

## Deliverables

- A working `npm run capture:scenes` producing one multi-scene WebM with fades plus the `--json` payload.
data.title: Multi-scene capture driver: one recorder, fades, single WebM

## Goal

As a player, when I change the Control Scheme in Settings and then leave and re-open Settings, the row must still show the scheme I chose. The operator reports that it reverts to Asteroids, i.e. the setting appears not to be saved at all.

## Operator report (verbatim)

> AH-0MVIMPC11001F7WU is still not working. It seems the setting is not being saved. 1) selecting settings and change to 4 directional 2) back to menu 3) open settings and the control profile is back to asteroids

Parent/related: discovered-from:AH-0MVIMPC11001F7WU (mid-run scheme honouring, implemented in commit 3c75eb4c, stage in_review) and AH-0MVI7LRCJ006Q8SA (the control-scheme setting feature).

## Investigation performed (2026-10-21, dev HEAD 60cd1f22)

The reported flow was reproduced end-to-end in a real headless Chromium against the actual game (dev server and a production build), driving the real UI by keyboard and by mouse, and inspecting the live Phaser scene state plus localStorage on every step:

- Menu -> Settings -> cycle Control Scheme to Four Directional -> Back -> Menu -> Settings again: the reopened row shows `Control Scheme: Four Directional`, and `ai_hell_settings.controlScheme` is `fourDirectional`. **Passes.**
- The same flow from the in-game pause menu (Play -> Esc -> Settings -> change -> Back -> Resume): stored value stays `fourDirectional`. **Passes.**
- Pause menu -> Settings -> change -> Back -> Quit to menu -> Settings: row shows Four Directional. **Passes.**
- Change in Settings -> Back -> Play: the spawned ship reports scheme `fourDirectional` (spawn-time application works). **Passes.**
- Production build (`npm run build` + `vite preview`), keyboard flow: same result. **Passes.**
- Mouse-driven flow (click the row, click Back, click Settings): same result. **Passes.**

Storage write trace confirms exactly one write per change, through `SettingsScene.setControlScheme` -> `_persist` -> `saveSettings`, with `controlScheme` set to the selected value. No code clears or rewrites the record. `npm run build` (incl. `tsc --noEmit`) passes.

## Conclusion so far

The defect is **not reproducible on current dev HEAD**. Most likely explanations, in order:

1. **Stale build in the test environment.** The deployed GitHub Pages site is built from `main` (latest tag v0.1.13) and its Settings screen has **no Control Scheme row at all** (verified against the live bundle: `Control Scheme` / the row glyphs are absent). If the operator tested the published site they cannot have changed the setting there; the only "4-Directional" toggle in the live bundle belongs to the dev/tuning Gym player panel, whose scheme toggle is config-driven (CSV) and only persists via that panel Save button.
2. **Stale local build**: an old `dist/` served via `npm run preview`, or a `npm run dev` started from an out-of-date worktree, or a cached page from before commit `d45df97c`.
3. **Storage scoping**: localStorage is per origin (scheme + host + port); a dev server on a different port or an incognito window would show defaults again.

## What is needed to progress

- Operator environment details: the URL (host:port) used, whether it is `npm run dev`, `npm run preview`, or the published Pages site, and the browser (including private/incognito).
- Immediate check in that environment: DevTools -> Application -> Local Storage -> `ai_hell_settings`, then confirm whether `controlScheme` is present and what value it has right after changing the row (before leaving Settings) and after reopening.
- If `controlScheme` is written as `fourDirectional` but the row still shows Asteroids, capture the browser console output — that would indicate a different fault (e.g. a second game instance or an older cached module) and we can then reproduce it.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: The reported environment is identified (URL/build) and the flow is reproduced there, or the operator confirms that with a fresh `npm run dev` from current `dev` the choice persists.
- AC2: If a genuine defect is found, a regression test proves the scheme survives leaving and re-opening Settings (menu and pause origins) and a fix lands; the existing coverage (`SettingsScene.test.ts` AC5 "the choice survives a reload", `PlayScene.controlScheme.test.ts`) is extended only where the new failure mode is not already covered.
- AC3: Full project test suite passes.
data.title: Control scheme reverts to Asteroids after re-opening Settings (operator report, not reproducible on dev HEAD)
